title: Ivory Coast name World Cup squad: Yan Diomande and Amad included, Nicolas Pepe earns recall
content:
Emerse Fae, the manager of the Ivory Coast national team, has announced his 26-man squad for the World Cup, with former Arsenal forward Nicolas Pepe being named in the selection alongside Yan Diomande and Amad.

Pepe, 30, was left out of the Ivory Coast squad for the Africa Cup of Nations last winter. Fae hinted that off-field issues were his reason for leaving the Villarreal forward out of his squad.

Pepe has had a productive season in Spain, scoring eight goals and eight assists to help his side — who are eighth in La Liga with two games to play — qualify for the Champions League.

The forward earned an international recall for Ivory Coast’s friendlies in March, where he came on as a late substitute during a 4-0 defeat to South Korea (March 28) and then scored the winning goal in a 1-0 victory over Scotland (March 31).

However, fellow former-Premier League winger Wilfried Zaha has been left out of the squad. The 33-year-old earned a surprise recall to the national team for the most recent edition of AFCON, representing the nation for the first time in over two years last December.

The former Crystal Palace winger, who plays for Charlotte in Major League Soccer, made three appearances at AFCON 2025 as Ivory Coast reached the quarter-finals but was not then selected for the March internationals.

The two highest-profile names in the selection are Diomande of RB Leipzig and Ousmane Diomande of Sporting CP. Leipzig winger Diomande, 19, has been scouted by a number of clubs, including Liverpool. The German side are widely reported to want around £85million (€98m) for the teenager.

Former Barcelona midfielder Frank Kessie, now playing his football for Al Ahli in the Saudi Pro League, has been the captain of the national team since 2024.

There is further Premier League involvement in the Ivory Coast squad in the form of Manchester United winger Amad, Nottingham Forest’s Ibrahim Sangare, and Crystal Palace’s Evann Guessand. Elsewhere in the squad, centre-back Emmanuel Agbadou joined Besiktas from Wolverhampton Wanderers in February while former Brighton & Hove Albion winger Simon Adingra joined Monaco in January on loan from Sunderland.

Sebastian Haller has been left out of the squad. The 31-year-old Utrecht striker has scored 11 goals in 34 appearances for the Ivory Coast, including the winning goal in the 2023 AFCON final. However, he has not played for the Ivory Coast since November 14 and missed the most recent edition of AFCON.

Uncapped Inter striker Anfe-Yoan Bonny, who only last week completed a switch of international allegiance having represented France at youth level, and Nice’s Elye Wahi have both been included. Wahi made a similar switch earlier this year.

Fae, 42, led Ivory Coast to winning the 2023 edition of AFCON. He was appointed interim manager of the side after Jean-Louis Gasset was sacked during the group stage of the competition. Fae had never taken charge of a senior side before.

Ivory Coast were drawn into Group E, where they will face Ecuador (June 15), Germany (June 20), and World Cup debutants Curacao (June 25).

Goalkeepers: Yahia Fofana (Caykur Rizespor), Mohamed Kone (Charleroi), Alban Lafont (Panathinaikos)

Defenders: Emmanuel Agbadou (Beşiktaş), Clement Akpa (AJ Auxerre), Ousmane Diomande (Sporting CP), Guela Doue (Strasbourg), Ghislain Konan (Gil Vicente), Odilon Kossounou (Atalanta BC), Evan Ndicka (AS Roma), Wilfried Singo (Galatasaray)

Midfielders: Seko Fofana (Porto), Parfait Guiagon (Charleroi), Christ Inao Oulai (Trabzonspor), Franck Kessie (Al-Ahli), Ibrahim Sangare (Nottingham Forest), Jean-Michael Seri (Maribor)

Forwards: Simon Adingra (Monaco), Ange-Yoan Bonny (Inter Milan), Amad Diallo (Manchester United), Oumar Diakite (Cercle Brugge), Yan Diomande (RB Leipzig), Evann Guessand (Crystal Palace), Nicolas Pepe (Villarreal), Bazoumana Toure (TSG Hoffenheim), Elye Wahi (OGC Nice)
